title: S(3;4,4,8) = 87
statement: The generalized off-diagonal Schur number S(3;4,4,8) is exactly 87: every 3-colouring of {1,...,87} contains x_1+...+x_{3}=x_4 monochromatic in colour 1, or x_1+...+x_{3}=x_4 monochromatic in colour 2, or x_1+...+x_{7}=x_8 monochromatic in colour 3; and some 3-colouring of {1,...,86} avoids all three.

concept_refs.note: generalized off-diagonal Schur number; no graph node authored yet
the additive-Ramsey case; off-diagonal is the analogue of asymmetric Ramsey numbers

provenance.conjectured_by: literature: T. Ahmed, D. Schaal, 'On generalized Schur numbers' (2015-2016), Conjecture: S(3;s,t,u) = s*t*u - t*u - u - 1 for 4 <= s <= t <= u. Still open as of arXiv:2604.11030 (Song and Mao, April 2026), which proves the companion conjecture but not this one. This value, 87, AGREES with the formula.

evidence.notes: Found by the CDCL core, then replayed by OffDiagonalSchur::first_violation (independent of the encoder) and cross-checked a second time against the FULL, unreduced solution-set list before being written.

Produced by axeyum's own proof-producing CDCL core (solve_with_drat_proof_streaming, ADR-0381) streaming TEXT DRAT to disk and re-derived in the same process by axeyum's own backward DRAT checker (check_drat_backward, ADR-0382). No external solver and no external checker took part. The deciding CNF is the SUBSUMPTION-MINIMAL encoding: for solution sets S subset of S', clause(S) implies clause(S'), so only the minimal antichain is emitted -- a SUBSET of the full clause list, so refuting it refutes the full instance. check-claim-certificates.py validates the stored CNF clause by clause rather than by byte-identity, which is the check the bound actually needs.

notes: REPRODUCES a published computed value. REPRODUCTION of an independently computed value. Song and Mao, arXiv:2604.11030 (13 April 2026), Table 3, report S(3;4,4,8) = 87 from their own exhaustive computer search with a conventional SAT pipeline. Our value agrees exactly, and unlike theirs it carries a machine-checked refutation. Both sides are discharged -- n = N-1 satisfiable with an independently replayed colouring, n = N refuted with a DRAT proof re-derived by axeyum's own checker. SOUNDNESS NOTE: colours here are NOT interchangeable (each forbids a different equation), so the usual whole-palette symmetry breaking is UNSOUND and would produce a wrong unsat. The encoding orders colour classes only within blocks of colours carrying the SAME equation, and crates/axeyum-search/tests/offdiag_schur.rs carries a negative control showing the unblocked version turning satisfiable S(3;3,4,5) at n=41 into unsat.
